findings.reason: §18's own thesis (one owner of the rule) is falsified by a site it omits, so §18 must name `followup_pointers.py` as a fourth consumer and route it through the predicate, exactly as it does for `implementable_sections`, `plan_executable_remainder` and `_implementable_section_ids`.
findings.text: §18 states the declaration map is read for "which sections are still work" by three readers and consolidates their inline `== "implementable"` comparison into one predicate, but `followup_pointers.py:150` (`followup_verdict`, returning `FollowupVerdict(True, "implementable-section")`) is a fourth site that applies the identical rule inline; the plan's predicate would leave a duplicate spelling alive, and the §18 done-when does not name it.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — s17 puts one deep module in `reckon/_plan_html.py`: a single raw-text parser hides heading span location, level, wrapper-id identity resolution and landed-card recognition behind `plan_headings` plus the `structured_section_spans` projection, replacing the store, the prose parser and the MCP view's separate walks.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — s18 centralises the "a section is still work" rule into one predicate on `reckon/_schema.py`, but its enumeration of the sites that spell the rule today misses `reckon/followup_pointers.py:150`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1477, cli_options 317, refusal_families 23; the sections that add public surface (s17 adds `plan_headings` and the machinery-element predicate, s18 adds the classification predicate) each name in their own text what they add and state why nothing can be retired, and none adds a CLI option, MCP view or refusal family (s16 states the refusal reuses the existing `plan-review-missing` family).
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the design sections s16–s18 name the existing machinery they extend or replace and cite it by file and symbol (`_StructuredSectionSpanParser` and `structured_section_spans` in `reckon/_plan_html.py`, `landed_section_ids` in `reckon/_store.py`, `section_record_id`/`section_id_candidates` in `reckon/crew/routing.py`, `plan_fingerprint`/`_fingerprint_forms`/`_AuthoredProseParser` in `reckon/crew/plan_review.py`, the three "still work" readers), each of which exists as described.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no section adds an unjustified layer: `section_record_id` gains one optional parameter in place, `structured_section_spans` is re-expressed as a projection rather than duplicated, and every new reader states why the existing mechanism cannot be extended instead (s17 cannot shrink the family because `structured_section_spans` and `landed_section_ids` keep external callers; s16 makes its coverage predicate module-private rather than a wrapper over `read_plan_review`).
